stanzas.alt: Sanaka and the sages approach Vaikuntha. The four divine sages Sanaka and his brothers travel to Vaikuntha to behold the Lord.
The sages pass the beautiful enclosures of Vaikuntha. The sages cross the enclosures and reach the incomparable abode amid the Naisreyasa garden, pools and jeweled mansions.
Jaya and Vijaya bar the sages at Vaikuntha’s gate. The two gatekeepers stop the sages at the entrance; anger rises in the sages by the Lord’s prompting.
The curse and the gatekeepers’ plea. The sages curse the gatekeepers to asura births; Jaya and Vijaya bow and seek pardon.
Narayana appears with Lakshmi and Garuda. Narayana comes forth with Lakshmi, one graceful arm resting on Garuda, and delights the sages with his beautiful form.
The gatekeepers surrender and receive assurance. Jaya and Vijaya take refuge at the Lord’s feet; he compassionately promises their return after three asura births.
Diti and Kashyapa conceive the two asura brothers at twilight. The two attendants are born to Diti and Kashyapa; their conception takes place at twilight.
The two brothers trouble the worlds. The two brothers, Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha, become hostile to the worlds and torment them.
Hiranyaksha roams the submerged world seeking an opponent. Unable to find an opponent, Hiranyaksha submerges the beloved earth and roams the worlds with his mace.

Varuna directs Hiranyaksha to seek Vishnu. Varuna tells Hiranyaksha that only Vishnu is a worthy opponent; the stanza closes by addressing the Lord as visible to devotees and asking him to remove illness.
